crons.name: morning-meeting-brief
crons.message: ⚡ EXEC DISCIPLINE: run any `python3 <path>` command exactly as written — a bare invocation, nothing appended, no shell wrapping, no chaining with other commands, no output redirection, no exit-code capture. Scripts always print one JSON line to stdout with a `status` field (ok/error/degraded); parse that final line to decide what to do. openclaw 2026.4.11 rejects complex shell invocations before they run. Generate and deliver the morning meeting brief. 1) Run: python3 ~/.openclaw/meetings-coach-workspace/scripts/gcal-fetch.py --days 2. Read the JSON output — these are today's and tomorrow's professional meetings. 2) Filter to real meetings only (is_real_meeting=true). 3) For each real meeting: a) Run person-bootstrap.py to create person files for new attendees. b) Run workflowy-sync.py --create-nodes to create Workflowy meeting nodes. c) Run meeting-prep.py --meeting-id EVENT_ID to assemble context (attendees, facts, open commitments). 4) Format the brief using the template in CRONS.md — factual schedule only: meeting times, attendees, locations, open commitments with attendees. Do NOT include talking points. Include a tomorrow preview. 5) Write the formatted brief to cache/morning-brief-ready.txt — this is the fleet-delivery cache file read by fix-it/morning-fleet-deliver at 12:00 UTC. Do NOT call timed-deliver.py; the fleet deliver cron handles the send. 7) Write result summary to ~/.openclaw/meetings-coach-workspace/cache/last-morning-brief.json as JSON: {"timestamp": "<ISO UTC>", "meetings_briefed": <N>, "status": "ok" | "error", "summary": "<one sentence>"}. DO NOT touch ~/Dropbox/openclaw-backup/agents/meetings-coach.status.md — the heartbeat cron owns that file.

crons.name: pre-meeting-alert
post-meeting-scan
crons.message:
⚡ EXEC DISCIPLINE: run any `python3 <path>` command exactly as written — a bare invocation, nothing appended, no shell wrapping, no chaining with other commands, no output redirection, no exit-code capture. Scripts always print one JSON line to stdout with a `status` field (ok/error/degraded); parse that final line to decide what to do. openclaw 2026.4.11 rejects complex shell invocations before they run. Scan for recently-ended meetings and new transcripts. 1) Run gcal-fetch.py and identify meetings ended in the last 60 minutes. 2) Run transcript-scan.py to fetch Krisp transcripts and match to meetings. 3) IDEMPOTENCY CHECK: For each pending debrief file in cache/pending-debrief-*.json, extract the event_id and grep ~/Dropbox/openclaw-backup/commitments/active.md for that event_id. If found: the debrief was already confirmed — delete the stale pending file and skip it. Do NOT re-present an already-confirmed debrief. 

4) KRISP 401 HANDLING. If transcript-scan.py reports "401 Unauthorized" or "Token verification failed" (or ANY Krisp auth error):
(a) Write cache/krisp-last-401.json with {"ts": "<current ISO UTC>"}. This marker is read by heartbeat.py to set krisp_auth: expired in the status file.
(b) Read cache/krisp-last-alert.json if it exists. It contains {"ts": "<ISO UTC>"}. Compute the age in minutes. If age < 90 minutes, DO NOT send another Telegram alert — return EXACTLY the empty string (zero bytes, no narration). The previous alert is still fresh.
(c) If age >= 90 minutes OR cache/krisp-last-alert.json does not exist: send Telegram '🐷🔍 Krisp transcript access returned 401 Unauthorized. The refresh_token is revoked. Run krisp-auth-manual.py locally and scp fresh tokens.json to ~/.openclaw/meetings-coach-workspace/cache/krisp-tokens/tokens.json.' Then write cache/krisp-last-alert.json with {"ts": "<current ISO UTC>"}.
(d) Do NOT continue to steps 5-6 — no transcripts are accessible. Write cache/last-post-scan.json with status: error, summary: krisp 401. Stop here.

5) If transcript-scan.py succeeded: read the output. If NEW items were extracted and staged (not already confirmed): send a debrief summary on Telegram with action items, decisions, follow-ups. Include '/confirm to save to brain · /dismiss N to skip item N'. Delete cache/krisp-last-401.json if it existed (recovered).

6) If no transcripts found and no pending debriefs: return EXACTLY the empty string (zero bytes, no narration — not even "NO output", "Done", "all clear", or a status summary).

7) COACHING (after debrief, if coaching.enabled is true in meeting-config.json): For each staged debrief that has transcript text, run: python3 ~/.openclaw/meetings-coach-workspace/scripts/transcript-metrics.py --event-id EVENT_ID. Read the metrics JSON. Read coaching.growth_areas from meeting-config.json. For each growth area, find Sam's utterances in the transcript that relate to that area. Compose a coaching message using the format in CRONS.md (metric header, 1-2 sentence assessment, quoted excerpt with timestamp, suggested alternative). Send ONE coaching message per debrief on Telegram. After sending, append to cache/coaching-history.json: {"event_id": "...", "meeting_title": "...", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "metrics": {...}, "area_assessments": {"concision": "strong|good|needs_work", ...}}.

8) Write result to ~/.openclaw/meetings-coach-workspace/cache/last-post-scan.json as JSON: {"timestamp": "<ISO UTC>", "transcripts_processed": <N>, "debriefs_staged": <N>, "unmatched": <N>, "status": "ok" | "error", "summary": "<one sentence>"}. DO NOT touch ~/Dropbox/openclaw-backup/agents/meetings-coach.status.md — the heartbeat cron owns that file.

crons.name: heartbeat
crons.message:
⚡ EXEC DISCIPLINE: run any `python3 <path>` command exactly as written — a bare invocation, nothing appended, no shell wrapping, no chaining with other commands, no output redirection, no exit-code capture. Scripts always print one JSON line to stdout with a `status` field (ok/error/degraded); parse that final line to decide what to do. openclaw 2026.4.11 rejects complex shell invocations before they run. Run: python3 /home/node/.openclaw/meetings-coach-workspace/scripts/heartbeat.py

This script checks auth state, reads cron caches, verifies required files, prunes stale preps, and writes meetings-coach.status.md automatically. You do NOT write the status file — the script does it.

Parse the JSON output. If `status` is `ok`: return EXACTLY the empty string (zero bytes, no narration — not even "NO output", "Done", "all clear", or a status summary). Any text you emit is logged and charges tokens even when no Telegram message is sent. If `status` is `degraded` or `error`: send the value of the `alert` field to Telegram verbatim. Do NOT write to meetings-coach.status.md yourself. Do NOT wrap or rewrite the script's output. Do NOT use python3 -c or heredocs. Just run the script and relay the alert field when non-ok.
